stem: A cell is observed depositing collagen-rich bone matrix and contributing to mineral deposition. Later, it becomes surrounded by that matrix and occupies a mature position within bone. Which of the following sequences of cell identities best explains these observations?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Osteoclasts resorb bone rather than first depositing its collagen-rich matrix. The observed matrix-forming cell is an osteoblast, which becomes an osteocyte when enclosed by the matrix.
options.misconception: Assigns initial matrix formation to bone-resorbing osteoclasts.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The cell begins with the matrix-forming role of an osteoblast. Its later enclosure corresponds to an osteocyte, not conversion into the bone-resorbing osteoclast lineage.
options.misconception: Misidentifies both the matrix-forming cell and its later enclosed state.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Macrophage-lineage cells give rise to osteoclasts involved in bone resorption. They do not explain the specified sequence of matrix deposition followed by enclosure as a mature bone cell.
options.misconception: Assigns the osteoblast-to-osteocyte sequence to the macrophage lineage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Osteoblasts produce bone matrix and contribute to mineral deposition. When an osteoblast becomes enclosed in that matrix, it becomes an osteocyte, matching the observed sequence.
options.misconception: No misconception: matrix-forming osteoblasts become osteocytes when enclosed.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Osteoclasts belong to the monocyte–macrophage lineage and resorb bone. This proposed sequence does not explain either the initial matrix-forming function or the later enclosed bone cell.
options.misconception: Uses a resorptive lineage to explain matrix deposition and cell enclosure.

context:
Learning objective: Distinguish the matrix-forming osteoblast and its osteocyte transition from the bone-resorbing osteoclast lineage.

Osteoblasts produce bone matrix and contribute to mineral deposition. When an osteoblast becomes enclosed in that matrix, it becomes an osteocyte, matching the observed sequence.
